name: stuck-pagination
description:
An Endpoint Central server that stops advancing and answers every `page` with the same full page of a thousand. The walk's two exits are an empty page and a short page, and this shape produces neither, so it used to spin until the task timed out with nothing in the log to say why.

The no-progress check is the working guard -- the CONFIG maxPages ceiling behind it (enforced by pager()) is ten million records deep and exists only so an adversarially rotating server still terminates, by raising rather than truncating silently. A page whose row ids match the previous page's means the server ignored `page` or replayed a cached response, and the walk stops on the first repeat and says so, which is what log_contains pins.

Every page carries a full thousand rows because a shorter page would end the walk on its own and prove nothing. Page one's first row is a real endpoint so the run still proves rows are parsed and reported; page two is a thousand rows with no resource_id -- different content, so the walk correctly continues -- and page three repeats it, which is the first genuine repeat and the stop.

metadata.total is served so the truncation message exercises its 'Retrieved x/y available assets' form rather than the no-total fallback.

The route matching page=4 exists ONLY as a terminator for a regression. Serving the stuck page with when_exhausted=repeat_last alone would make an unguarded walk run to a 10,000-page ceiling and fail this scenario by timing out rather than by failing an assertion; with the terminator, an unguarded walk stops one request later and fails on request_count, requests_absent and the missing log line instead.

namespaced_ids is skipped for the reason recorded in happy: the id is the bare Endpoint Central resource id with no server scope.

log_contains: endpoint-central: pagination stopped making progress at page 3; the server repeated the previous page. Retrieved 1/2500 available assets
